items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-19
items.q: this is how I met people like Danny Barker, for instance... and I didn't identify the name with the person until I met him backstage at Nixon's Grand, and Red Allen, and people like that.

ctx.x: So, I called Bechet and he suggested Sidney D. Paris and Gate Mouth. And so, I just made a deal with him to bring him in. And, in fact, it was Sidney who taught me the procedure. He says, well, you send us the tickets. And as soon as we get the tickets, we'll consider that a firm commitment and we'll come in. You see. So, we set the time and I got some local musicians that I already knew from Philadelphia. And so, everything came together. And in 1936, in the beginning of 1936, we had the jazz concert where…
Did you have, in producing these concerts, did you have a stake more in the New Orleans musicians than you did in others? Or did you do?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there... I had met Louis before... Albert went to introduce me to him.

ctx.x: And it was a black theater and I used to come out of, out of class and go across the street to the theater all the time, because I knew a lot of the musicians that were, that were playing in the, in the show. And it was during the time when I had first started doing jazz concerts. So it was 1936 and I went backstage, because his band was playing there. And I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there, Al Nicholas. So, I had, I had met Louis before, I don't actually remember when, but…
Okay, we're on the second reel. Al Rose, same date. August 13th, 1989. Okay, we left off with Eus... Eus Panassia.
